data.narrative:
Gilmour Space Technologies is a Series D-stage space and aerospace company that has raised approximately A$100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 4 private peers at Series C/D stage within Space & Aerospace, supplemented by reference to 5 public sector comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and an additional 8 private companies for directional context.

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. The 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Sierra Space ($8.0B, Series C), Apex Space ($2.3B, Series D), Varda Space Industries ($1.5B, Series C), and Skyryse ($1.1B, Series C)—yield a median valuation of $1.9B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (23.9x median across the 6-ticker sector set) cannot be applied due to the absence of target revenue disclosure, which is typical for private companies. Revenue data would be necessary to leverage this secondary method.

The triangulated range is $1.6B–$2.2B, centered on a median of $1.9B. This single-method result carries concentration risk; material upside to the range would require either (i) validated revenue and margin data to calibrate public multiples downward or (ii) access to transaction comps at later vintages. Key uncertainties include stage-premium sensitivity (Gilmour is the only Series D in the peer set) and the wide dispersion in the comparables themselves, particularly Sierra Space's $8.0B outlier position.
